newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine should reform tax system - George Soros.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine should reform tax system - George Soros.

text.p: American financier and philanthropist George Soros said on Friday that Ukraine was in dire need of a reformed tax system if it hoped to improve its economy.

"We have to create the environment where enterprises and economic activity can be conducted in the official economy, where taxation is not as oppressive," Soros told Reuters while visiting Ukraine for an economic conference.

Soros, 66, who emigrated from Hungary to England in 1947 and then to the U.S. in 1956, made his fortune in his new home and since then has dedicated portions of his earnings to helping countries with emerging economies.
He stressed the need to reduce regulations and licenses required to operate a business in Ukraine.

"Each time you have a license, it is a licence to extract money bribes from the people who have to get the licence," he said. "It's very important to reduce the amount of regulations, and then to reduce the level of taxation."

Ukraine's unwieldy taxation system has at times resulted in businesses being taxed for 100 percent of profits, and has been blamed for the former Soviet republic's large shadow economy, estimated at up to 40 percent of all economic activity.
President Leonid Kuchma promised this week to reform the tax system next year, which would include lower taxes and fewer regulations.
"Having a lower rate but more people paying it, that's really the task," said Soros.
Soros, who has contributed millions of dollars to various charitable projects in Ukraine, said the country has made economic progress, such as bringing hyperinflation to heel.
But he said it still faces large problems such as a shortage of energy resources and the money to pay for them, and the need to reduce government expenditures.
